title: The Smallest Word With a Given Length and Letter Sum

concept.title: Fill the word from the right with the largest letters, keeping every earlier position at least `a`
body: Give each letter a value: `a = 1`, `b = 2`, ..., `z = 26`. Among all words of **length `n`** whose letters add up to **`k`** (a word always exists when `n <= k <= 26 * n`), print the **alphabetically smallest** one. For `n = 3` and `k = 27` the answer is `aay`: `1 + 1 + 25 = 27`, and nothing smaller exists. For `n = 5` and `k = 73` it is `aaszz`.

To make a word smaller alphabetically, make its **left** letters as small as possible, even at the cost of the right letters. So push as much of the sum as possible to the **right**: go from the last position to the first. At the position `i` (counting from 0) there are `i` positions before it, and each of them needs at least `1`, so the letter here can be at most `k_left - i`. Take the largest possible letter, `min(26, k_left - i)`, and subtract it from `k_left`.

body.code:
k_left = k
letters = [0] * n
for i in range(n - 1, -1, -1):
    c = min(26, k_left - i)       # the earlier i positions keep at least 1 each
    letters[i] = c
    k_left -= c
print("".join(chr(96 + c) for c in letters))

body: The result looks like `aaa...a`, then one middle letter, then `zzz...z`. The earlier positions end up with exactly 1 because the sum that remains for them is just enough. The algorithm is O(n), and the output is built with one pass. (A different but equal way is to go from the left and give each position the smallest letter after which the rest can still reach the sum.)

statement: Letters have the values `a = 1`, `b = 2`, ..., `z = 26`. Print the alphabetically smallest word of length `n` whose letter values add up to `k`. It is guaranteed that such a word exists.
inputFormat: One line with `n` and `k`: the number of letters and the letter sum.
hints: Make the leftmost letters as small as possible.
Go from the last position to the first.
At the position i the letter is min(26, remaining sum - i).

explanation: The word is filled from the last position to the first; each position gets the largest letter that still leaves at least 1 for every earlier position.

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n, k = map(int, input().split())

left = k
letters = [0] * n
for i in range(n - 1, -1, -1):
    c = min(26, left - i)
    letters[i] = c
    left -= c
print("".join(chr(96 + c) for c in letters))
